_comment: FLAT AllToAll on the NIC-per-GPU variant: 4 hosts x 2 GPUs = 8 GPUs, each GPU carrying its own 100Gbps NIC into its host's leaf, 2 leaf + 2 spine switches (16 fine nodes). Same 4 hosts and same 2:1 taper as the other two, doubled in fabric width because each host now presents two ports. Completes the set: mini_1gpu_1nic (no host tier), mini_2gpu_1nic (host tier as a mandatory funnel), this one (host tier as an OPTIONAL relay, since a GPU can reach the fabric without crossing it).
_expected: T* = 0.64 s = 8 epochs, set by the LEAF CUT: 16 GB per direction (4 GPUs x 4 remote GPUs x 1 GB) against 2 x 100Gbps = 25 GB/s -> 0.64 s. The per-GPU egress bound is slacker at 6 GB / 12.5 GB/s = 0.48 s, and intra-host peer traffic is 1 GB / 25 GB/s = 0.04 s. THE MULTIPATH CHECK: delete one spine and T* must rise to 1.28 s = 16 epochs, an exact 2x; every cross-leaf demand should show up split across both spines, since neither alone can carry the cut. Note this variant is the FASTEST of the three despite matching mini_2gpu_1nic's GPU count -- twice the NICs doubles the leaf-spine cut, halving the binding bound from 1.28 s to 0.64 s. That gap is the price of the shared NIC, measured.
_hierarchical_note: hierarchical is false here, but unlike mini_2gpu_1nic it need not be: this topology's .topo file marks its 4 hosts as cells (the GPUs own their own external links, so _build_cell accepts them). The flat solve is kept as the GROUND TRUTH -- 16 fine nodes is small enough to solve directly -- so that a hierarchical run on the same file has something to be validated against rather than only self-consistency-checked. To make that run, set hierarchical true, add a hierarchy_prefix, and expect a makespan at or ABOVE the 0.64 s here; below it means one of the two is wrong.
_why_alltoall: Under AllGather the volume crossing the leaf cut depends on routing, so the cut bound is soft and the spine tier can go slack. Under AllToAll every chunk has a unique destination GPU, so the 16 GB per direction is pinned by the demand matrix however it is routed, making the cut bound EXACT.
_epoch_note: epoch_duration is PINNED to 0.08 s (= 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, one GPU's NIC), the same value as the other two inputs so all three are read on one clock. FASTEST_LINK would size it from the 200Gbps intra-host PCIe link instead (0.04 s), doubling the epoch count for no gain. 0.08 s divides the 0.64 s bound exactly, so nothing is lost to the final ceiling.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. There is no Python class for this topology and none is wanted. The path is relative to the repo root.
